title: Performance Evaluation of Vertical Flow Constructed Wetlands Treating Institutional Wastewater With Supporting ANN‐Based Prediction
content:
At the National Institute of Technology Delhi, vertical-flow constructed wetlands planted with Canna indica were tested for institutional wastewater treatment using gravel, sand or a combination of the two. The gravel–sand configuration achieved the highest pollutant removal. Artificial neural network models were used to predict phosphate and total nitrogen removal, and the predictions were compared with measured values.


ABSTRACT

Constructed wetlands (CWs), particularly vertical flow constructed wetlands (VFCWs), offer a sustainable option for decentralised wastewater treatment owing to their low energy demand, simple operation and robustness under variable loading conditions. However, predicting pollutant removal efficiency remains challenging because of the non-linear interactions among hydrological, physico-chemical and biological processes. This work evaluates the treatment performance of three VFCW configurations—gravel (CWG), sand (CWS) and gravel–sand (CWG + S) media—receiving institutional wastewater and develops an artificial neural network (ANN) model to predict pollutant removal efficiency from routinely monitored influent and operational variables. Among the tested configurations, CWG + S achieved the highest average removal of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), phosphate and total nitrogen (TN), with efficiencies of 90.34%, 86.72%, 81.20% and 75.70% respectively. The ANN model, implemented as a multilayer perceptron, reproduced the observed removal efficiencies with high predictive skill, yielding coefficients of determination (R 2) greater than 0.90 for the target pollutants in both training and validation datasets while maintaining low root mean square error and Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency values close to unity. Sensitivity analysis of the trained network indicated that influent pollutant concentration and wastewater temperature were the most influential predictors of removal efficiency, followed by hydraulic retention time. These findings demonstrate that coupling VFCWs with ANN-based prediction provides a reliable data-driven tool for performance assessment, design support and operational optimisation in decentralised wastewater treatment systems.
